title: Knowledge check: Understanding Node.js and npm

questions.prompt: In Understanding Node.js and npm, which statement best describes Node.js runtime and event loop?
options: Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Use asynchronous I/O for waiting work, but remember synchronous CPU-heavy functions still block the event loop. Bound concurrent work and honor cancellation, streams and backpressure.
Make the runtime version, module system, package scripts and lockfile explicit. A fresh installation should reproduce the same dependency graph and documented startup behavior.
questions.answer_key: Use asynchronous I/O for waiting work, but remember synchronous CPU-heavy functions still block the event loop. Bound concurrent work and honor cancellation, streams and backpressure.
questions.explanation: Use asynchronous I/O for waiting work, but remember synchronous CPU-heavy functions still block the event loop. Bound concurrent work and honor cancellation, streams and backpressure.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Understanding Node.js and npm?
options: Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
questions.answer_key: A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.
questions.explanation: A dependable project starts with a supported Node.js runtime, a lockfile, explicit module-system choices, and repeatable npm scripts. Run the same startup command from a clean checkout and record version assumptions.

questions.prompt: A change related to Understanding Node.js and npm appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
